title: Inside GI-TOC's Whistleblowing Framework
report_title: A window for reform? Rethinking the UNTOC review mechanism after COP13
summary: Maya and Daniel examine the official Whistleblowing policy released by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime. They break down who can report, the strict rules around confidentiality versus anonymity, the designated intake channels, and how internal investigations are structured.

title: Inside GI-TOC's Whistleblowing Policy
summary: Maya and Daniel break down the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime's formal whistleblowing policy. They examine who can report, the explicit protections and reporting channels, how investigations are conducted, and the institutional governance designed to safeguard integrity.

title: Inside GI-TOC's Whistleblowing Framework
summary: Maya and Daniel break down the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime's formal whistleblowing policy. They examine the scope of reportable misconduct, the strict rules around confidentiality and anonymous reporting, the specific reporting channels, and how investigations and governance oversight are structured.

title: Where Next for the UNTOC? The Future of the Palermo Convention
report_title: The GI-TOC at the 13th Conference of the Parties to the UNTOC
summary: Maya and Daniel examine a briefing from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime on the future of the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC). They explore the structural delays in the convention's review mechanism, the data gap in the Global South, and the political and financial challenges facing multilateral efforts at COP13.

title: Kinship, Crime, and the Clan Debate in Germany
summary: Maya and Daniel unpack a landmark report from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime examining Arabic-speaking criminal networks in Germany. They explore the roots of long-established Mardin-origin clans, the rise of newer Syrian networks, and what law enforcement often gets wrong about kinship and organized crime.

title: Mapping Colombia's Revived Caribbean Cocaine Corridors
summary: Maya and Daniel dissect a comprehensive report from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC) on how Colombian cocaine trafficking routes through the Caribbean are reviving to supply booming European markets. They explore the internal transport corridors, maritime smuggling methods, corruption dynamics, and regional geopolitical shifts detailed in the investigation.

title: Inside the Western Cape Gang Ecosystem
summary: Maya and Daniel break down Issue 10 of the Western Cape Gang Monitor by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime. They explore why military deployment under Operation Prosper is faltering, how incarcerated bosses run syndicates from their cells, the violent expansion of gangs into rural towns like Malmesbury, and the landmark trial exposing state armouries supplying the underworld.

title: Crime at a Crossroads: Eastern and South-Eastern Asia
report_title: Global Organized Crime Index 2025 - Continental overview
summary: Maya and Daniel unpack the 2025 Global Organized Crime Index report from GI-TOC focusing on Eastern and South-Eastern Asia. They examine the stark regional contrasts, the explosion of industrial cyber-scam compounds and human trafficking, and the world's widest resilience gaps.
